questions.solution_html:
• Effect of oxygen availability on meat colour
  • • Myoglobin is the principal pigment responsible for meat colour.
  • • In the absence of oxygen, deoxymyoglobin gives meat a purplish-red appearance.
  • • When the package is opened and meat is exposed to oxygen, oxymyoglobin forms and
  • produces a brighter red colour.
  • • During prolonged storage, metmyoglobin may accumulate and produce brown
  • discoloration.
  • • Therefore, purple meat in an unopened vacuum pack is not necessarily spoiled.

• Effect on microbial growth
  • • Removing oxygen inhibits many aerobic spoilage bacteria, including Pseudomonas
  • species.
  • • It may favour the relative growth of lactic acid bacteria and other organisms that tolerate
  • low oxygen.
  • • Vacuum packaging does not destroy microorganisms already present in the meat.
  • • Certain anaerobic pathogens, including Clostridium botulinum, may present a risk under
  • unsuitable storage conditions.
  • • Proper refrigeration, hygiene, shelf-life control and validated processing are essential.

questions.question: Select the factor most likely responsible for excessive drip loss after thawing of a frozen fish product: a). Repeated freezing and thawing b). Proper rapid freezing c). Good glazing d). Constant frozen storage / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Effect on lipid oxidation
  • • Oxygen promotes the oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids in meat.
  • • Lipid oxidation produces peroxides and secondary compounds that can cause rancid
  • odours and flavours.
  • • Vacuum packaging reduces oxygen exposure and generally slows lipid oxidation.
  • • Consequently, it can help preserve flavour and nutritional quality during storage.
  • • Oxidation is reduced, not completely prevented.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

• Relationship between oxygen and colour stability
  • • Oxygen exposure affects the chemical state of myoglobin.
  • • High oxygen exposure may initially improve the bright red appearance but can also
  • promote oxidative deterioration.
  • • Low oxygen maintains deoxymyoglobin and limits oxidation, producing a darker purple-
  • red colour.
  • • Colour changes must be assessed along with odour, texture, package condition and
  • microbiological safety.

questions.question: Describe how protein denaturation contributes to microbial inactivation during HPP. a). Nutrients increase. b). Spores are formed c). Proteins become more active. d). Enzymes lose activity and metabolism stops / [CO3] [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Cooling and packaging: The powder is cooled and packed in moisture-resistant, airtight
  • packaging.
  • Flow chart
  • Egg selection → Breaking → Filtration → Pasteurization → Concentration (optional) →
  • Atomization → Spray drying → Powder collection → Cooling → Packaging.
  • Advantages
  • • Long shelf life when properly processed and stored.
  • • Reduced weight and volume.
  • • Convenient transportation and storage.
  • • Easy to measure, handle and reconstitute.
  • • Useful in bakeries, confectionery, pasta and food manufacturing.
  • Limitations
  • • High initial equipment cost.
  • • Heat may cause protein denaturation or functional changes.
  • • Moisture absorption can cause caking during storage.
  • • Improper processing may reduce product quality or safety.
